newsitem.title: FRANCE: Congolese troops said to be firing at each other.
newsitem.headline: Congolese troops said to be firing at each other.

text.p: Congolese soldiers are firing on one another in the streets of the capital Brazzaville, the commander of French forces in the central African nation said on Sunday.

"The problem is that there are (former president Denis Sassou) Nguesso's militias and there are Congolese army units which are not under the control of their officers, and so we have seen Congolese troops firing on their fellow soldiers," Commander Alexis Jaraud said.

"There is shooting in the streets, and they are using rocket-launchers in residential neighbourhoods," Jaraud told French television LCI by telephone from the French forces' Pelican air base in Congo.
He said there had been looting in Brazzaville since Friday.
Brazzaville has been shaken for the past four days by fighting between supporters of Nguesso and soldiers loyal to President Pascal Lissouba and other political and ethnic rivals.
